scope: Three faithful-servant originals reviewed at original detail for hand contact, contrast and continuity.
globalConditions: Unnamed parable figures and precise household details are artistic interpretation.
Technical review is not owner approval or final browser acceptance.

entries.alt: A steward in a blue tunic hands a filled bowl to an older woman while two other household members hold their meals.
entries.caption: The steward places food into another person's hands. Jesus describes a faithful servant entrusted with feeding the household at the proper time; responsibility becomes care for the people before him.
entries.findings: Bowl transfer is supported naturally from both sides; overlapping hands remain distinguishable with plausible fingers and wrists. Steward's face-directed attention reaches the woman. Other bowl grips and figures are coherent. Natural skin, woven tunics, pottery and courtyard fit the intended ancient setting.
conditions: Exact meal, household composition and gestures are illustrative; do not invent relationships among the figures.

entries.alt: A seated man raises a hand toward three people holding bowls while keeping a cup beside his own food.
entries.caption: A contrasting steward keeps his attention on his own table while others wait. This restrained scene pictures neglected care alongside Jesus' warning about a servant who uses his master's delay as permission to mistreat the household.
entries.findings: Different bald moustached steward clearly distinguishes this contrast from the faithful blue-clothed man. Raised dismissal hand, cup grip, bowls and waiting postures are coherent. Expressions convey disregard and concern without sensational violence. Source includes mistreatment and self-indulgence; image illustrates part of that warning, not every narrated act.
conditions: Do not narrate this as the faithful steward's later downfall or a single man's biography.
Do not claim visible intoxication or assault; neither is shown.
Body size or baldness must not be used in the caption as evidence of moral character.

entries.recommendedTitle: Found serving when the master returns
entries.alt: The blue-clothed steward holds bread beside a meal table and turns toward an older man standing in the open courtyard entrance.
entries.caption: The returning master finds the steward still serving the household. Jesus calls that servant blessed: the master's arrival reveals the faithful work already underway.
entries.findings: Steward's salt-and-pepper curls, moustache, blue tunic and shoulder cloth match scene 01. Courtyard and eating household figures sustain continuity. Older clean-shaven master is distinct, and reciprocal eye direction is credible. Bread grip, satchel strap hand, lower hand and meal contacts remain natural. Photographic detail and plausible period materials.
conditions: The arrival setting and expressions are artistic visualization; do not claim a visible formal reward or promotion in this moment.
